body:
## Summary

```diff
 local across / if_any / if_all inside inline functions
- quote written ... or ..1 as the column selector
+ capture expanded forwarded arguments during execution
  apply existing column exclusions and share dependency checks
```

Preserve ordinary R dots forwarding through inline summary functions without
evaluating their summaries during static planning. Unnamed top-level
`across(...)` has a separate expansion boundary, tracked in #1151. Closes #1138.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `(function(...) dplyr::across(..., sum))("x")` returned 6 under
  dplyr but failed with `'...' used in an incorrect context` at the public
  Margin verb; `..1` failed as a nonexistent column.
  **After:** 432 ordinary-dplyr comparisons pass across data.frame, tibble and
  data.table; wrapper/function controls, evaluation order, grouping exclusions,
  output collisions and contextual-share dependency refusals also pass.
- Verification: [full check for `3a416559`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1149#issuecomment-6592980769), 198/198 test files, **0 ERROR / 0 WARNING / 0 NOTE**.
- Review: [round 1 for `4cfe65aa`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1149#issuecomment-6573645605);
  [round 2 for `8af91298`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1149#issuecomment-6574329416),
  [round 3 for `a98fee97`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1149#issuecomment-6574679398),
  [round 4 for `0df69707`](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/pull/1149#issuecomment-6574977041).

- CI follow-up: compare ordinary class-combination refusals, cover static callee proofs, and synchronize job deadlines with workflow contracts. No new code-review round ran for `3a416559`; the prior review remains pinned to `0df69707`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The code and regression tests can be reverted together.

**Blast Radius:** summaries

Inline local summary selection calls forwarding bare `...` or a `..n` selector
use runtime promise capture before the existing selection rewrite. Unnamed
top-level `across()` retains dplyr's expansion path.

An omitted ordinary formal forwarded separately as a function argument remains
a limitation: current main errors, and this branch can return a value that
differs from dplyr. The reproduction and default-argument distinction are
tracked in #1154.
